goal: Select an OCR method that preserves long-ſ (U+017F), æ, œ, u/v, i/j diplomatically for the DR 1582/1609/1610 Roman/Antiqua scans, replacing the ſ→f stock-tesseract 'ocr_consensus' scaffold (§6.2/6.3 defect).

ground_truth.page: nt-1582 jp2_idx 0028 = Matthew 1 (verses 1–15 on this leaf; ends catchword 'Mathan')
ground_truth.reference: s-dismas render_archaic surfaces (ſ-preserving transcription, independent of the archive.org scan) for scripture/matthew/1/1–15

source_resolution_finding.implication: Both scan lines are inherently ~70–72 dpi. Word-accuracy ceiling ~0.8 fold even for SOTA models is a SOURCE property, not a model failure. Honest per-region/per-book confidence variation (aim #4, the canonical error map) is therefore a genuine deliverable, not a defect to hide.

design_constraint.rule: spelling_glyph_model.py §6.1: archaic forms must be restored from the WITNESS, never from a lossy inverse of the modern text.
design_constraint.consequence: Rule-based ſ re-insertion onto a ſ-normalized reading (e.g. CATMuS output) is FORBIDDEN — it fabricates orthography. For the 199 gap-book verses (no archaic transcription witness), the ONLY ſ witness is the scan glyph itself, so the method MUST natively preserve ſ. This disqualifies ſ-normalizing models (CATMuS, script/Latin) for gap-book rendering.

candidates_scored.note: Comparative on the SAME page vs GT v1–15. fold=word-accuracy (ſ→s folded); dipl=diplomatic-form recall (unfolded); ls_word=fraction of GT ſ-words read VERBATIM with ſ; ls=count of ſ emitted. Input=2x Lanczos unless noted.

results.verdict: good words but LSTM normalizes ſ→s/f even with dawgs off; NOT diplomatic
ſ-preserving (positive control) but Fraktur letterform bias caps Roman-type word accuracy
legacy engine collapsed on this 70dpi scan; unusable
BEST raw word reading + reads ſ as CORRECT s (not f) + emits period abbrevs (ꝯ,¬), but NORMALIZES ſ→s — disqualified by design constraint for gap books
WINNER — near-top word accuracy AND native ſ preservation (dipl==fold: ſ in correct positions, no penalty); u/v preserved; design-compliant

winner.input_scale: 2x Lanczos upscale of the 70dpi scan (fold 0.779; 1x=0.750/ls_word 0.909, 3x=0.779/ls_word 0.818 — scale within noise, 2x fastest)
winner.throughput: ~14–32 s/page single-threaded on CPU (segmentation-dominated) — full-tome run is multi-hour; parallelize + resumable-cache like ocr_fulltome.py
winner.rationale: Best BALANCE of word accuracy (0.78, ~tied CATMuS 0.81, above Fraktur 0.72) and native diplomatic ſ (0.73–0.91 ls_word). A CATMuS-family Latin model that KEEPS the long-s. Qualitative body read genuinely diplomatic: 'the ſonne of Dauid', 'Iſaac', 'Naaſſon', 'Tranſmigration', u/v preserved. Errors are proper-noun confusions at 70dpi + right-margin annotation bleed (a region-typing job for P4.2).
